messages:
emma: Quick heads-up: after landing the adaptive-kernel-selector yesterday, production ingest shows a regression on short-chat flows. p50 up ~9%, p95 up ~20%. Traces point to increased syscall + nano-write overhead.
rahul: saw that. I pulled a few host traces. There's a spike in user-space tokenize CPU and a massive bump in writev counts from the sidecar.
isabel: any change related to tokenizer?
emma: yes 10: we swapped to per-request tokenizer instances to avoid cross-request state. That eliminated a lock but removed the shared tokenizer pool. For tiny requests that's +0.8-1.5ms per req.
ci-bot: deploy 2026-03-20T22:10:02Z - feature adaptive-kernel-selector rolled to 30% traffic.
rahul: flame snippet from a hot host (60k traces sampled):
```
request.parse_body 0.6ms
host.tokenize_single 1.2ms
kernel.select_dynamic 0.7ms (oscillates)
kernel.exec_opt 2.7ms
kvcache.lookup 0.5ms (backend hits up, but eviction_rate +18%)
sidecar.writev 0.9ms (avg 12 syscalls/request)
```

isabel: kernel.select_dynamic seems to flip kernels for seq 32-64 depending on microbatch size. Kernel churn causes cache pressure + CPU scheduling noise.
syl: small note on transport: http2 framing + gRPC produce many 40-120B DATA frames for streaming chat chunks. Each frame triggers sidecar write. That's the syscall explosion.
rahul: Also the microbatcher heuristic now emits smaller batches under tail traffic patterns. Effective batch_size median fell from 6->3 for short flows. That amplifies kernel switches and increases per-token overhead.
emma: TL;DR contributors: 1) tokenizer pool removal; 2) adaptive kernel selector oscillation on short seqs; 3) microbatcher shrink on tail patterns; 4) raw streaming writev fragmentation.
isabel: suggested experiments: A) reintroduce small shared tokenizer pool for <64 token requests (lock-free pool) B) pin kernel for seq<=48 for 24h canary C) adjust microbatcher min_window to prefer batch_size>=4 D) coalesce streaming frames in sidecar up to 256 bytes or until flush.
syl: coalescing note: we need to be careful to not delay EOS/finish events. Implement threshold-based coalescing with immediate flush on finish or user-initiated flush. Should be safe.
rahul: I can toggle kernel pin quickly with runtime flag. Will run a 2h canary and collect p50/p95.
emma: I'll prototype a tokenizer pool patch (lockless ring) and bench on microbench harness. Expect to regain ~1.0ms per-request.
isabel: I'll change microbatcher config in staging: min_window 6ms -> 10ms to force slightly bigger batches. We'll measure median impact.
ci-bot: perf job queued (job=6087655000) comparing baseline vs adaptive-kernel canary.
rahul: quick numbers from a smoke run with kernel pin + coalesce (local): p50 -2.5ms, p95 -10ms on short-chat scenario; syscall count down 65%.
syl: nice. Plan: incremental rollout. 1) enable sidecar coalescing feature-flagged (owner: syl) 2) kernel pin runtime toggle for short seqs (owner: rahul) 3) tokenizer pool reintroduce (owner: emma) 4) microbatcher min_window adjust in canary (owner: isabel) 5) add new metrics: sidecar_syscall_count, tokenizer_allocs, kernel_flip_rate (owner: isabel)
emma: I'll add an e2e microbench that simulates tail traffic to validate microbatcher change.
rahul: also adding an alert: kernel_flip_rate > 3/s/host -> page oncall.
isabel: timeline: we'll roll coalescing + kernel-pin to 5% canary tonight after tests. If p95 improves, ramp to 25% tomorrow.
syl: coalescing implementation notes: keep an in-memory buffer per-stream, flush on size>=256B or at 2ms heartbeat, or on finish. Unit tests + integration tests required.
ci-bot: perf comparison job=6087655000 started. Results ETA ~1h.
emma: thanks team. Let's hold other global rollouts until we confirm rollback isn't needed. Post results when perf job completes.
rahul: got it. Im opening PR for kernel pin + flag now.
isabel: I'll instrument the sidecar metric endpoints so we can graph syscall counts by host.
syl: adding coalescing flag to sidecar config namespace. Will send patch link when ready.
ci-bot: created ticket INF-3219 to track follow-ups.
